record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Let T : ell^infinity(N) -> ell^infinity(N) be a bounded linear operator with dense range. Must T be surjective?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N})$ denote the Banach space of bounded sequences of real (or complex) numbers, equipped with the supremum norm. Suppose $T : \ell^\infty(\mathbb{N}) \to \ell^\infty(\mathbb{N})$ is a bounded linear operator whose range $T(\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N}))$ is dense in $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N})$. Must $T$ be surjective?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was resolved in the negative: there exist injective bounded linear operators on $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N})$ with dense, non-closed (hence proper) range, constructed via injective Tauberian operators on $L_1$. This appears in work of W. B. Johnson and collaborators (arXiv:1408.1443), showing that dense range does not imply surjectivity on $\ell^\infty$.

status_evidence.title: Injective Tauberian operators on L_1 and operators with dense range on ell_infty
status_evidence.snippet: There are injective, non surjective operators on ℓ∞ that have dense range.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a counterexample: a bounded linear operator on ℓ∞ that has dense range but is not surjective, answering the question negatively.
